subject.title: Feature: Add maxTurns/maxToolCalls config option to limit agent iterations

question: Should OpenClaw expose an opt-in global/per-agent hard iteration budget, and if so should its canonical unit be tool-calling rounds, individual tool invocations, or separate named limits?
rationale: The counter unit, defaults, subagent inheritance, and forced-response behavior become public config and runtime contracts; code inspection can identify viable implementations but cannot choose those permanent semantics safely.

options.title: Sponsor one round budget
options.body: Adopt an opt-in tool-calling-round budget with explicit parent/subagent limits and deterministic final-response behavior, then require the linked PR to implement and prove that single contract.

options.title: Expose separate counters
options.body: Support distinct model-round and individual-tool-call limits, accepting a larger config and testing surface for more precise operator control.

options.title: Keep heuristic guards only
options.body: Decline a new hard-budget surface and continue improving tools.loopDetection and timeout behavior, closing the candidate PR after documenting that direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor one round budget
recommendation.body: Adopt an opt-in tool-calling-round budget with explicit parent/subagent limits and deterministic final-response behavior, then require the linked PR to implement and prove that single contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history and prior review route the existing loop-detection config, enforcement, and public contract through this owner most directly.
